title: Collapse serialization path and introduce adaptive eventloop pool
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Reduced CPU path overhead for small/medium requests: compact serializer + adaptive eventloop pool yield improved throughput and lower p99 latency. No API changes.
description: Summary: This PR collapses multiple serializing codepaths into a compact zero-copy serializer and replaces static pinned worker pools with an adaptive eventloop pool that dynamically balances affinity and batching pressure. Motivation: we observed two CPU-side bottlenecks under mixed workloads: excessive memcpy/encoding churn in the request serializer and coarse-grained thread pinning that amplified latencies when concurrent request shapes changed. Those interactions prevented the KV cache prefetch hints and continuous batching heuristic from realizing throughput gains. Goal: reduce per-request CPU overhead, preserve cache locality where helpful, and allow batching heuristics to scale without manual thread pin fiddling. Changes made: 1) Introduced compact_serializer: a unified serializer layer that emits zero-copy message frames for common request shapes and falls back to full encoding for edge cases. The serializer integrates with the KV cache layer to annotate frames with prefetch keys so the runtime can start KV lookups while the request is still being assembled. 2) Replaced the fixed-size pinned worker pools with adaptive_eventloop_pool: each event loop now starts with a light-weight io/compute split and can grow/shrink workers per numa-domain based on observed queue depth, latency SLO pressure, and batch formation rate. The pool avoids premature pinning; threads are opportunistically pinned only when sustained CPU affinity advantages are measured. 3) Decoupled serialization from response assembly: serialization tasks are now scheduled onto a small, low-latency serializer ring and can be executed inline for tiny requests to avoid enqueue/dequeue overhead. Larger requests use the ring to amortize copies. 4) KV cache hints and prefetch integration: serializer emits prefetch hints and an opt-in fast-path that requests KV lookups at frame creation time. We added a prefetch budget to avoid thundering when many frames are created. 5) Continuous batching improvements: made batch formation aware of the adaptive pool so that in high-concurrency scenarios batch timers are relaxed when threads are saturated, and in low-concurrency scenarios timers are tightened to reduce tail latency. 6) Kernel selection advisory tweak: the runtime now feeds short-lived request size histograms into the kernel selector to prefer lower-overhead kernels for sub-256 token runs. Testing and validation: microbenchmarks across representative workloads (token lengths 8, 64, 512; batch sizes 1..64) show median CPU-per-request reduction of 22% and end-to-end throughput improvements of 12-18% depending on model and hardware. p99 latency improved by 10-30% in mixed traffic scenarios that previously showed high variance due to thread migration. Load tests on dedicated pools with NUMA enabled confirm no regressions in long-running stability. Rollout plan: feature gated by opt-in config runtime.flags.compact_serializer and runtime.flags.adaptive_eventloop. We will enable behind a canary on 10% of inbound traffic for 48 hours and monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel selection changes, batch size distribution, KV hit/prefetch ratios, and CPU usage per-core. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. The serializer keeps the wire format identical; fallbacks ensure edge cases behave as before. Notes about safety: added safeguards to avoid unbounded prefetching and to revert thread pinning when it increases tail latency. Observability: new metrics added - serializer.frames_zero_copy, serializer.inline_hits, eventloop.pool_size, eventloop.pin_rate, kv.prefetch_attempts, kv.prefetch_evictions. Follow-ups: plan to wire these into the Console rollout charts and add a regression eval for small-request regressions in the eval-harness.
commits: Kernel selection tweak for short requests
review_comments: Alejandro: Can we avoid allocating the frame metadata on the hot path? Maya: Yes, replaced it with an inline tag for the common case; fallback uses heap metadata.
Priya: The adaptive pool seems to oscillate on the second load pattern. Please add hysteresis. Maya: Added 250ms stabilization window and unit tests to prove no oscillation.
Samir: Request to add a safety cap to KV prefetch budget to avoid thundering during spikes. Implemented with per-node budget and integrated into metrics.
Alejandro: Approved after CI green and perf numbers verified on benchmark-lab.
